U.S. Department of Energy (2015). Quadrennial Technology Review 2015, Chapter 6: Innovating Clean Energy Technologies in Advanced Manufacturing. Technology Assessment 6.I: Process Heating. U.S. DOE, Washington, DC. Published as an appendix to the 2015 QTR (https://www.energy.gov/quadrennial-technology-review-2015); some references were accessed April-May 2016, so the assessment file was finalised in 2016.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 1). A qualitative R&D assessment: it prints no capex, opex, efficiency, specific energy consumption or lifetime for any technology. Main file (2 technologies): the Queen City Forging infrared billet-preheating furnace (direct-heater_electric) with output temperature lower bound (above 800 degF) and availability lower bound (downtime under 5%), and the steam-based heating temperature ceiling (most systems below 500 degF) on boiler_fuel-fired; temperatures converted from degF to degC with the formula. Measures file: three printed % savings (IR billet heating 75%, HEPHAISTOS microwave curing up to 75%, microwave-enhanced ethylene cracking 30-50% expected). Other-values: Table 6.I.1 (2010 process heating energy use and losses by industry), Table 6.I.2 (typical temperature ranges in degF and 2010 energy use by process heating operation), Table 6.I.3 (national energy and CO2 savings opportunities by technology area), and shares of fuel, steam and electricity. Not loaded: Table 6.I.4 (qualitative electrotechnology list), Table 6.I.5 (heat exchanger material grades), Table 6.I.6 (R&D project list), microwave/RF/induction frequency bands. Traps: Table 6.I.2 temperatures are in degF (column header 'F'); the IR case study's 75% is printed as 'more energy efficient', which could mean a saving or an efficiency gain. Almost all numbers are reprinted from the 2010 MECS-based AMO footprints and project reports.
